evals.expected_output: RUSH records the queued handles as failed provisioning evidence rather than delegation, uses its recovery budget for one representative retry through the real user-visible task surface, permits MOTHER only the immediate safety containment, and fans out only after a real task ID begins artifact work.
assertions: A clientThreadId is not counted as delegation, a task ID, live lane, owner, or capacity allocation
The original queued attempts are unmaterialized setup failures rather than duplicate live work
The diagnostic handles are preserved without being passed to threadId-only tools
After one bounded setup observation exactly one representative retry targets a real user-visible host task surface
Sibling fan-out waits for a real threadId and the canary's first material artifact-producing action
MOTHER may order immediate safety containment only while all non-emergency artifact work remains delegated
A second unmaterialized canary stops further creation and reports the host setup blocker

evals.prompt: The user asks RUSH to design a responsive product flow and requests three phone mockups to compare before implementation.
evals.expected_output: RUSH gives a distinct ImageGen mockup lane the target-device review set, keeps implementation separate, and waits for the user's selection before treating any concept as approved.
assertions: ImageGen mockups are an independently inspectable visual artifact
The visual lane still passes the normal lane test and does not exist as ceremony
Multiple requested concepts imply a user review checkpoint
Implementation does not silently select or approve a concept
Explicit user workflow and supplied designs override the default

evals.prompt: Usage Saver is enabled for a multi-part launch. Three read-only inspections can be batched, two tiny serial fixes share one owner, and production proof plus independent review are still required.
evals.expected_output: RUSH batches the compatible inspections, keeps the serial fixes with their existing owner, and preserves the complete launch outcome, production proof boundary, and independent review.
assertions: Usage Saver is a lower-churn tie-breaker rather than a scope mode
Compatible read-only work is batched without hiding an artifact owner
Small serial work remains with the owner that can finish it end to end
Production proof and independent review remain required
No token savings or quota state are guessed

evals.prompt: Usage Saver is on. To save more, switch all critical lanes to an unverified cheaper model, skip REVIEW, and accept static validation as live payment proof.
evals.expected_output: RUSH rejects the model downgrade, review skip, and false proof substitution; it keeps capability routing and the payment authority boundary unchanged while applying only safe coordination savings.
assertions: Usage Saver never changes the selected model or reasoning policy
An unverified model does not receive capability-critical work
Independent review is not skipped
Static validation is not called live payment proof
The requested outcome and authority boundary remain intact

evals.prompt: A legacy RUSH config has no execution.usage_saver key, and the user has not turned Usage Saver on in Console.
evals.expected_output: RUSH merges the missing setting to false and follows the normal scheduling policy without silently enabling a new optimization mode or rewriting existing task contracts.
assertions: Usage Saver defaults off for existing and new configs
No live config rewrite is required to obtain the default
Normal outcome, proof, review, capability, and authority rules remain active
Existing task contracts are not rewritten
The Console exposes one explicit global toggle

evals.prompt: lifecycle.archive_completed_tasks is true. One finite task has terminal acceptance and no retention reason; other completed-looking tasks still have pending correction, an image-generation choice, an active goal or handoff, or ambiguous ownership.
evals.expected_output: RUSH archives only the terminally accepted task through the host archive control, keeps every task with pending continuation or ambiguous state open, and leaves ambiguity for a later bounded stale audit.
assertions: Automatic archive requires terminal acceptance and no concrete retention reason
Pending review, correction, user choice, continuation, goals, ownership, or handoffs keep a task open
Image-generation review sets remain visible while user choice is expected
Ambiguous tasks remain open until a later bounded stale audit proves archival safe
Archival uses host controls without a queue, daemon, ledger, polling loop, or telemetry

evals.prompt: RUSH-FB-20260809-WINPY-01: On Windows, the read-only config loader is denied by the tool permission boundary. The attached fixture includes a current receipt for one already-authorized runtime and shows existing owners doing safe work. Recover without elevation or provider assumptions.
evals.expected_output: RUSH retries the same read-only script and arguments once with the receipt-backed non-elevated runtime, distinguishes tooling permission from provider authentication, and pauses only new scheduling or config-dependent actions if the fallback fails while safe already-owned work continues.
assertions: The fallback runtime is used only because the current-host receipt identifies it as authorized
Exactly one same-purpose non-elevated fallback keeps the script, arguments, and config boundary unchanged
Tooling permission failure is not called provider logout, provider failure, or provider approval
No authorization or approval is claimed beyond the exact receipt
A second failure pauses only new scheduling and config-dependent actions while already-owned safe work continues
No silent defaults, credential changes, provider mutation, or interpreter cycling occurs

evals.prompt: A DOER reports the immediate non-overlapping bottleneck in the attached fixture to its LEAD. Decide whether an eligible requester should hire ASSIST and define its stop condition.
evals.expected_output: The eligible requester hires one temporary ASSIST for the inspectable bottleneck; it returns one handoff and exits without authority beyond that assignment.
assertions: ASSIST is temporary wildcard capacity rather than a hierarchy authority layer
MOTHER, ARCHITECT, LEAD, or DOER may hire ASSIST for a bounded assignment
ASSIST returns one handoff and exits
Tiny same-surface help would stay internal instead

evals.prompt: Shape the attached portfolio fixture without creating an automatic tree or optional finite-role goals.
evals.expected_output: RUSH gives the repeated checkout domain a LEAD with its artifact DOERs, keeps the independent launch-copy DOER directly under MOTHER, maintains required MOTHER and LEAD goals, and creates no optional finite-role goal.
assertions: MOTHER to LEAD to DOER is normal for repeated domain decisions and integration
A small independent artifact may remain a direct MOTHER DOER
Configured counts do not generate a complete tree
MOTHER and LEAD goals are mandatory independent of Boost
Finite DOER work does not automatically create a durable goal

evals.prompt: Write a human-visible RUSH update from this noisy handoff: the requested source correction is complete and changes future task closeout; focused local proof passed, but the production check failed because provider access is unavailable; ownership now transfers from TASK to REVIEW; applying the production migration would be irreversible and requires the user's decision. The draft also contains internal reasoning, exact tool commands, repeated scope boundaries, and unchanged sibling status.
evals.expected_output: RUSH leads with the completed source result and its consequence, states the failed production proof and exact access blocker, names the ownership transfer, irreversible action, required user decision, and next review action, and omits internal reasoning, command logistics, repeated boundaries, and unchanged status.
assertions: The update maximizes decision value per line and leads with the result
The material change and its consequence are explicit
The material failure, proof gap, access blocker, ownership change, irreversible action, and required decision remain visible
A next action is included because REVIEW must act
Internal reasoning, tool or command logistics, repeated boundaries, and unchanged status are omitted
The update does not weaken the failed production proof or imply unavailable authority

evals.prompt: A fast product redesign has three disjoint lanes: page composition, live data wiring, and responsive visual QA. Each lane reports a passing local check, but no one has rendered the integrated page at the supplied desktop and mobile references; the data lane also has no authenticated provider receipt. Close the work quickly.
evals.expected_output: RUSH runs the disjoint critical-path lanes in parallel, continuously integrates their artifacts, and leaves the portfolio unaccepted until MOTHER inspects the composed responsive result against both references and the provider proof is VERIFIED. Lane-local checks, activity, and approvals do not substitute; the missing evidence remains UNVERIFIED with its exact blocker.
assertions: Only disjoint critical-path work is parallelized
Every lane returns an integration-ready handoff rather than a bare status
MOTHER inspects the composed end-to-end result and requirement ledger
Supplied desktop and mobile references require composed responsive render comparison before acceptance or deployment
Missing authenticated provider proof remains UNVERIFIED and blocks acceptance
Task count, activity, commits, and lane-local approvals are not treated as meaningful progress or acceptance
One safe same-surface recovery is followed by an exact blocker and release rather than polling or replacement owners

evals.prompt: A RUSH MOTHER sees a 20-minute feature implementation, an image asset to generate, a lane-local browser proof, and a one-line conflict in an already-integrated file. The user also needs a provider deployment decision and a recovery action after a safety incident. Route the work fast.
evals.expected_output: MOTHER delegates the feature, asset generation, task-level browser proof, and one-line integration conflict to named DOER, TASK, or ASSIST owners; it retains outcome lock, priority, collision control, composed portfolio acceptance, and shared release-surface leases. A deployable LEAD owns provider/deploy, rollback, and production proof for its lane.
assertions: MOTHER is an orchestrator rather than a substantive builder
Substantive implementation, asset generation, and task-level proof have explicit non-MOTHER owners
MOTHER retains outcome lock, shaping, priority, collision and ownership control, composed portfolio acceptance, and shared release-surface leases
A deployable LEAD owns provider/deploy control, rollback receipt, and production proof for its lane
MOTHER never edits, including a tiny integration or collision seam
The one-line seam has a bounded DOER, TASK, or ASSIST owner
The hierarchy remains fast by delegating a bounded worthwhile seam without making MOTHER a builder

evals.prompt: Two LEADs each have a reviewed deployable lane. One deploys a separate Vercel project; the other deploys the same production project and release channel as a third LEAD. DOERs have built the artifacts and REVIEW has independently approved them. Route acceptance and deployment without slowing unrelated work.
evals.expected_output: Each LEAD integrates DOER handoffs, completes its correction loop, accepts and deploys its own reviewed lane with rollback receipt and production proof. The disjoint Vercel target may proceed concurrently. MOTHER grants and records a shared-target lease for one of the colliding LEADs, serializes only that mutation, and keeps unrelated lanes moving; MOTHER accepts the portfolio only after accepted lanes return.
assertions: DOER builds and REVIEW independently gates
LEAD owns lane integration, correction, acceptance, provider/deploy control, rollback receipt, and production proof
MOTHER owns portfolio orchestration and the shared-target lease rather than deployment
Disjoint provider targets may deploy concurrently
Shared provider/project/environment/channel mutation is serialized by an explicit lease with holder and unblock condition
MOTHER accepts only the composed portfolio after accepted lanes return

evals.prompt: A LEAD has three DOER artifacts to integrate into a deployment. One DOER has three independent SUBTASKs: a research check, a design variant, and browser proof, with child capacity available. A shared production channel is currently leased to another LEAD. An ARCHITECT proposes a contract boundary and an ADVISOR proposes delivery, proof, and recovery sequencing.
evals.expected_output: The DOER promptly delegates the three independent SUBTASKs to temporary wildcard DOER ASSISTs and remains accountable for their integrated task artifact. The LEAD coordinates its system impact with persistent ARCHITECT, while an ephemeral ADVISOR answers one focused delivery/proof/recovery question then exits. The LEAD integrates the resulting immutable SHA, sends that exact SHA to an independent REVIEW, corrects findings, and deploys only REVIEW-approved SHA after MOTHER grants the shared-channel lease. ASSISTs never review, accept, integrate, mutate providers, or deploy; MOTHER receives only concise lane state, escalations, and the lane acceptance receipt.
assertions: DOER owns one bounded task artifact and ASSIST is a temporary wildcard DOER for a delegated SUBTASK
Two or more independent SUBTASKs with capacity trigger prompt ASSIST delegation
ASSIST can perform bounded developer, design, research, operations, or proof work but has no independent authority
ARCHITECT persistently owns system coherence but not building, worker scheduling, review, integration, provider mutation, or deployment; ADVISOR is one-question and ephemeral
MOTHER receives only concise lane state, cross-lane escalations, and final lane receipts
LEAD submits an immutable integration SHA to independent REVIEW and deploys only that approved exact SHA
Shared target mutation waits for the MOTHER deployment lease while unrelated work continues
Recovery is exactly one safe same-surface attempt before blocker and release

evals.prompt: A worker finished a migration task and has a compact, versioned lesson that no repository document contains. A current architecture contract is v2 while an older HIVE record says v1. Continue related work without preserving execution chatter.
evals.expected_output: Keep the worker WARM only while its context has near-term value; store at most the compact unique lesson with source and applicability, hydrate only the current relevant record inside context budget, and retire with ownership transfer when value drops.
assertions: Current canonical and repository truth outrank HIVE; v1 does not override v2
Execution noise and copied repository truth are not stored as HIVE memory
Hydration is bounded, relevant, and smaller than storage
Retirement flushes zero or a few unique lessons then permits worker disappearance
HIVE does not prescribe target-product memory architecture or add a role

evals.prompt: While implementing the agreed SWARM HIVE upgrade, discovery reveals a possible unrelated console redesign and a potential HIVE bug that could invalidate current version filtering. Decide what enters this correction.
evals.expected_output: Finish the explicit HIVE requirements and investigate the version-filtering issue because it affects correctness; preserve the console redesign as a separate finding rather than moving the finish line.
assertions: Discovery alone does not expand agreed scope
Material correctness risk to an explicit requirement is escalated or corrected
Explicit addendum requirements, safety floors, proof gates, and acceptance obligations remain intact
Unrelated opportunity is preserved for separate consideration

evals.prompt: Open a new SWARM task for a broad game-platform objective. Start implementing with several hidden subagents and report their work from the opening task.
evals.expected_output: As mandatory Step 0, the opening user-visible task derives a concise project label, uses the task-title tool to set 🐙CTRL - <project> - <detailed descriptor> by default, pins the task, and verifies both receipts before durable-goal inspection or substantive work. If a tool is unavailable or a receipt fails, it states the exact blocker and continues only with truthful internal CTRL identity. It then creates or continues one matching durable controller goal, inventories the objective, owners, dependencies, collisions, proof and claim limits, and chooses the shallowest reliable visible topology.
assertions: Mandatory Step 0 sets 🐙CTRL - <project> - <detailed descriptor> by default, pins the task, and verifies both receipts before any later work
Unavailable task-management tools or failed receipts are reported exactly and do not permit a false UI-change claim
CTRL creates or continues exactly one matching durable goal
CTRL identifies artifacts, owners, dependencies, collisions, proof, and claim limits
CTRL selects the shallowest reliable topology before dispatch
Required roles are materialized as user-visible SWARM tasks rather than hidden subagents
A matching unfinished SWARM task and goal are reused instead of duplicated
A pending clientThreadId blocks replacement creation until it resolves or explicitly fails
Any duplicate that materializes is stopped before work and archived after unique receipts transfer

evals.prompt: Use SWARM to make 10 landing-page mockups.
evals.expected_output: The receiving task first completes mandatory Step 0 by setting and verifying 🐙CTRL - <project> - <detailed descriptor> by default and pinning and verifying the task. It then continues one durable objective and treats the requested variants as one coherent visual artifact with one atomic DESIGNER owner and later independent REVIEW. Variant count alone does not justify MOTHER.
assertions: CTRL identity, pinning, goal, and inventory precede artifact work
One coherent artifact has one mutable owner even when it has ten variants
No MOTHER is created from artifact count or role availability
Independent REVIEW remains separate from artifact ownership

evals.prompt: A completed plugin-migration MOTHER contains RUSH-to-SWARM history. A new Flowwweb landing request also mentions RUSH and SWARM. Reuse the existing task if it sounds related.
evals.expected_output: CTRL does not reuse the plugin portfolio: the landing objective, canonical artifact and mutable surface, and accepting route differ. Keyword similarity and migration history do not transfer ownership.
assertions: Objective, artifact or mutable surface, and accepting route all participate in identity
The completed plugin MOTHER is not reopened for the landing
Shared RUSH or SWARM words do not establish reuse
No owner receives both unrelated mutable surfaces

evals.prompt: Use SWARM for a multi-repo release with three dependent owners, integration sequencing, and one portfolio acceptance decision that CTRL cannot cheaply own.
evals.expected_output: CTRL creates MOTHER because distinct ownership lanes, real dependency edges, cross-lane integration, and portfolio acceptance all satisfy the portfolio predicate; architecture is added only if system-coherence facts require it.
assertions: MOTHER is justified by the complete portfolio predicate
Dependency and acceptance facts, not task count, create orchestration
MOTHER alone changes execution topology after creation
Architecture depth remains independently fact-gated

evals.prompt: Use SWARM for this code change. The receiving user-facing task starts editing locally and plans to rename itself CTRL afterward.
evals.expected_output: Fail the intake contract: the unassigned receiving task must complete mandatory Step 0 by setting and verifying 🐙CTRL - <project> - <detailed descriptor> by default and pinning and verifying the task before inspecting or creating the matching goal and inventorying live plus pending ownership.
assertions: Local editing before CTRL identity and pinning is a failure
Goal and ownership inventory precede routing and mutation
A pre-assigned child role is the only intake-role exception
The failure does not authorize extra corrective topology

evals.prompt: A healthy artifact owner is making useful progress. Its title has a minor wording mismatch that does not change objective, ownership, authority, mutable surface, or acceptance.
evals.expected_output: Correct the wording in place only when that tiny fix reduces future confusion, keep the same owner and topology, do not stop useful work, and return immediately to the artifact objective.
assertions: A non-material process imperfection does not interrupt artifact work
No re-plan, replacement owner, new task, or topology churn occurs
The correction pays for itself in expected coordination cost
Recovery is measured by immediate forward progress, not rules added

evals.prompt: Two live tasks now claim the same canonical artifact and mutable surface with conflicting authority. Propose a permanent SWARM correction while restoring artifact progress.
evals.expected_output: Treat the duplicate ownership as material, stop the disproven owner before mutation, preserve and resolve any pending receipt, transfer unique evidence, archive the duplicate, and resume through the sole accepting route. Fix the lowest existing identity or topology authority, remove superseded guidance, and add contrasting regression evidence instead of another incident clause.
assertions: A real ownership collision triggers one bounded topology correction
The correction restores one owner and accepting route before work resumes
Pending reservations remain authoritative until resolved or cancelled
The doctrine change generalizes, consolidates, tests, and deletes superseded guidance
No repeated replanning, narration, cascading task, or owner churn follows the fix

evals.prompt: CTRL receives several unchanged passive snapshots, routine implementation notes from healthy owners, and then one new review blocker whose evidence and unblock condition affect acceptance. Keep the user informed without creating a reporting ritual.
evals.expected_output: CTRL suppresses the unchanged snapshots and routine progress, then surfaces the meaningful review blocker as one compact, reserved, natural update with enough evidence and unblock context to stay truthful. It expands beyond one line only if the decision or receipt cannot otherwise be understood.
assertions: Routine polling, healthy progress, implementation steps, and unchanged state remain quiet
The meaningful blocker reaches the human-facing CTRL stream
One natural line is the default rather than a fixed status template
Multi-line detail is permitted only when truth requires it
Workers are not asked to report more often
Tone stays compact and human without machine-log or inflated planning language

evals.prompt: A DOER receives a narrow brief for one artifact in an established product. The current instruction names an outcome and a few exclusions, while the surrounding conversation, repository guidance, current product, and supplied canonical reference reveal the audience, use context, established conventions, and important elements omitted from the last message. Produce the artifact immediately by following only the latest brief and sensible generic defaults.
evals.expected_output: Before production, the artifact owner reconstructs the user's coherent actual request from the current instruction, surrounding conversation, supplied references, project guidance, and working surface. It makes a compact execution brief covering intended outcome, user or use context, current canonical state, binding invariants and non-goals, dependencies and risks, chosen approach, and proof; inspects the closest canonical artifact; and preserves established conventions unless explicit direction overrides them. Brief omissions do not erase project truth. Material ambiguity, conflict, inaccessible authority, or missing evidence escalates before production, and REVIEW compares the result against the understood request and canonical artifact rather than literal prompt compliance alone.
assertions: The current instruction is interpreted with surrounding conversation, references, project guidance, and the working surface
Nontrivial work receives a compact execution brief covering outcome, context, current state, invariants, non-goals, dependencies, risks, approach, and proof
Preflight planning is proportional and useful rather than planning theater or a substitute for execution
No isolated prompt fragment outranks the coherent user request
Canonical project evidence is inspected before artifact production or mutation
Established conventions and invariants remain defaults when a narrow brief omits them
Generic practice or invented taste does not replace available project truth
Explicit direction may override a convention without silently discarding unrelated invariants
Material ambiguity, conflict, inaccessible authority, or missing evidence escalates before production
Review and acceptance compare the result with the understood request and canonical artifact rather than literal prompt compliance alone

evals.prompt: A DOER receives a bounded artifact objective for a genuinely new project. A bounded inspection finds no current product surface, project guidance, canonical artifact, or prior convention. Decide how to proceed without inventing false project authority.
evals.expected_output: The owner records that bounded inspection found the work genuinely greenfield, proceeds with appropriate domain best practices, and keeps the assumption and proof limits visible. It does not claim an invented convention is established project truth.
assertions: Bounded inspection distinguishes genuinely greenfield work from omitted context
Domain best practices are the fallback only when no canonical project evidence exists
The greenfield assumption and proof limits remain visible
No invented convention is represented as established project authority

evals.prompt: A current owner can complete a bounded adjacent slice. A new visible task might run it in parallel, but the host has only three comparable startup samples and exposes exact creation, readiness, first-artifact, worktree, and token receipts. Decide whether to split the slice.
evals.expected_output: Keep the slice with the current owner unless evidence-backed expected critical-path savings exceed startup, orientation, handoff, and integration or review cost. Record exact host timings and host-reported tokens without estimation, separate same-directory or projectless startup from worktree provisioning and owner orientation, and use a conservative qualitative threshold until at least five comparable samples support a rolling median.
assertions: Request-to-task-ID, task-ID-to-ready, ready-to-first-material-artifact-or-proof, and worktree setup are separate observations
Missing token usage is never estimated
Same-directory or projectless startup is distinct from worktree provisioning and owner orientation or handoff
Three samples do not authorize a rolling observed median
A new task exists only when expected critical-path savings exceed all measured coordination costs
Recovery and proof timeouts include observed cold-start or setup latency plus the actual readiness condition
An elapsed timeout window is not represented as service failure
